topIssues.title: Resuming a paused goal never restores its recurring check-ins
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Pausing a goal with a recurring cadence, or changing its cadence kind and back, permanently loses its check-ins. Sync dismisses the slot's task while it's unwanted. When the goal is active again, sync finds that dismissed task under the slot's key and skips it, and scheduling under the same key replays the dismissed row. The active goal has no check-in, and nothing reports it.

**Expected**

Resuming a goal, or restoring its cadence, brings its check-ins back. A check-in the owner dismissed stays off.

Fix: #33641

topIssues.title: MESSAGE delivery preference fails to record once a person is reached from a second world
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

After MESSAGE `op=send` reaches a person, the delivery-preference component (fixed id per entity and agent) is written through `upsertComponent` with the message's `worldId`. The SQL adapter keys that upsert on the world, so reaching the same person from a second world inserts the fixed id again: a duplicate primary key. A message without a world uses an invented world id, which violates the `worlds` foreign key. The preference never moves past the first world, and every such send reports an error. Reproduced on real PGlite.

**Expected**

One delivery preference per person, updated by every successful send.

Fix: #33630

topIssues.title: Moving a one-time goal away and back to its date drops its check-in
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Since #33493 keyed one-time goal check-ins by their date, moving a pending one-time goal to another date and then back (an undo, or correcting a typo) leaves it with no live check-in. The original task was dismissed by the sync and still holds the date's key, and the sync never revives a dismissed slot. Reported on #33493 by @attentionhead and @fadhelcarlos.

**Expected**

Moving the date back restores the check-in, while a check-in the owner dismissed stays off.

Fix: #33614

topIssues.title: Calendar update/delete targets the wrong all-day event in calendars west of UTC
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

In `calendar-handler.ts`, `calendarEventLocalDate` (update/delete target selection) and `formatCalendarMoment` (all-day labels) read an all-day event's UTC-midnight `startAt` as an instant in the event's own time zone. For calendars west of UTC they read the previous day. In a New York calendar, "delete the field trip on November 1" targets the November 2 all-day event. Reported on #33499 by @lww0134-ctrl; Google all-day events were already affected.

**Expected**

All-day events are selected and labelled by their civil date, as the calendar views read it.

Fix: #33609

topIssues.title: Model dispatch detaches provider cancellation from the turn when an explicit signal is present
topIssues.author: Guo-Yixin
topIssues.body:
## Problem

`AgentRuntime.useModel` checks both a caller-supplied `params.signal` and the owning streaming context's `abortSignal` before and after dispatch, but forwards only the explicit signal to the provider when both exist. Cancelling the turn while a cooperative provider is waiting on a response body therefore leaves the transport running. Runtime cancellation is only noticed after that handler eventually settles.

Reproduced against `develop` at `4039228dfdd965354cb61a9da0e26774de21ae02`, through the real runtime and a real local HTTP response body. This is transport/lifecycle evidence with a deterministic registered model handler, not a live LLM call.

## Reproduction

1. Register a `TEXT_LARGE` handler that calls `fetch(url, { signal: params.signal })` and awaits `response.text()`.
2. Have the local HTTP server flush a partial body and hold the response open.
3. Call `runtime.useModel` with an explicit caller controller inside `runWithStreamingContext({ abortSignal: turnController.signal }, ...)`.
4. After the server receives the request, abort only `turnController`.

The handler's signal remains un-aborted and the pending response is not cancelled. Aborting the explicit caller controller subsequently allows cleanup. Caller-only, turn-only, shared-signal, and pre-aborted controls behave correctly.

## Expected behavior

The provider transport should observe cancellation from either owner, without mutating the caller's request or aborting the other owner's controller. Cancellation must retain its reason and must not trigger provider fallback.

## Proposed scope

Compose the two distinct signals once at the dispatch boundary and use the same signal for provider parameters, runtime checks, downstream delivery, and embedding validation. Preserve signal identity when there is only one signal or both references are the same. Add real-runtime HTTP regressions and document the cancellation contract; no provider plugin API or dependency changes.

The new cancellation suite on the unchanged baseline is **1 failed / 6 passed**; after the implementation it is **7 passed**. The existing provider fallback suite also passes (**18 tests combined**). Full package and repository verification are being recorded separately, including any Windows limitations.
